**Anthony Albanese**
The Labor Party prime minister who governs from Canberra. He defeated Scott Morrison's Liberal-National Coalition in 2022 and won reelection in 2025. His government includes Foreign Minister Penny Wong, who pledged at a 2022 Pacific Islands Forum meeting in Fiji to "end the climate wars."

**Kevin Rudd and the Stolen Generations apology**
In 2008 Labor Prime Minister Kevin Rudd issued a formal National Apology to the "Stolen Generations," the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children who were forcibly taken from their families under government policies. Albanese later appointed Rudd ambassador to the United States.

**Liberal-National Coalition**
The long-standing center-right alliance of the Liberal and National parties, the main rival of the Labor Party. It governed under John Howard, Malcolm Turnbull, and Scott Morrison. In 2025, its reversal on a policy to end public servants' work from home helped it lose ground to Labor.

**Robert Menzies and "The Forgotten People"**
Menzies was Australia's longest-serving prime minister and the founder of the modern Liberal Party. His 1942 radio speech "The Forgotten People" praised the middle class as the backbone of the nation.

**Hopetoun Blunder and Edmund Barton**
When Australia federated in 1901, Governor-General Lord Hopetoun first asked New South Wales premier William Lyne to form the government. Lyne could not win enough support, so Edmund Barton became Australia's first prime minister instead.

**Scott Morrison and the Black Summer bushfires**
The 2019–2020 bushfires burned huge areas and killed vast numbers of animals, including koalas and kangaroos, and their smoke nearly disrupted the Australian Open tennis tournament. Prime Minister Scott Morrison was criticized for vacationing in Hawaii during the crisis. After his surprise 2019 election win, he had claimed that the "quiet Australians" had won.

**One Nation and Pauline Hanson**
One Nation is a far-right, anti-immigration party led by Pauline Hanson. After Hanson won a Senate seat in 2016, Labor senator Sam Dastyari mockingly invited her to share a "halal snack pack."

**Offshore detention on Nauru and Manus Island**
Australia has sent asylum seekers who arrived by boat to processing centers on Nauru and on Papua New Guinea's Manus Island. The Guardian's "Nauru files" database documented abuses there, and the Manus center was later shut down.

**Malcolm Turnbull and the Trump phone call**
In a tense early 2017 call, Liberal Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull pushed President Donald Trump to honor an Obama-era deal for the U.S. to resettle about 1,250 refugees from Australia's offshore centers. Turnbull also tried to change the words "insult" and "offend" in Section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act.

**Uluru Statement from the Heart**
A 2017 declaration by a National Constitutional Convention of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander delegates at Uluru. It called for an Indigenous "Voice" to Parliament enshrined in the constitution and a Makarrata Commission to oversee truth-telling and treaty-making.

**Juukan Gorge destruction**
In 2020 the mining company Rio Tinto blew up rock shelters at Juukan Gorge in Western Australia, a sacred Aboriginal site with evidence of about 46,000 years of human occupation. The resulting outcry forced CEO Jean-Sébastien Jacques to resign.

**Harold Holt and "All the way with LBJ"**
Liberal Prime Minister Harold Holt expanded Australia's role in the Vietnam War, declaring support for the U.S. with the slogan "All the way with LBJ." He mysteriously disappeared while swimming off Cheviot Beach in 1967, and his body was never found.

**Novak Djokovic deportation**
In January 2022 the Serbian tennis star was deported from Australia before the Australian Open because he was unvaccinated against COVID-19 and did not meet the country's entry requirements.

**2025 election and the teal independents**
In Albanese's 2025 reelection, "teal" independents (socially liberal, climate-focused candidates in formerly Liberal seats) kept up their success. Clive Palmer's Trumpet of Patriots party flopped, and veteran ABC election analyst Antony Green retired from election-night broadcasting afterward.

**AWB oil-for-food scandal**
Under John Howard's government, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), a major supplier of food to Iraq under the UN Oil-for-Food Programme, was found to have paid millions of dollars in kickbacks to Saddam Hussein's regime. The scandal came to light in 2006.
